Score the coherence of topics

Source: R/evaluate.R
coherence.Rd

coherence() scores the coherence of each topic of a fitted model: whether the top terms of the topic tend to occur in the same texts. A topic whose terms co-occur is more likely to be interpretable as one subject than a topic whose terms rarely appear together, and coherence is the usual intrinsic measure of topic quality, computed from the corpus itself without external judgments.

Each topic is scored from its top n_terms terms and the co-occurrence of those terms in the modeled units (documents, or segments of a segmented model). Two measures are available: normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI; Bouma 2009), the mean over term pairs of how much more often two terms co-occur than expected, bounded between -1 and 1; and UMass coherence (Mimno et al. 2011), the mean log ratio of the number of units holding both terms of a pair to the number holding the higher-ranked one, usually negative. For both, larger values are more coherent. The result is a table with one row per topic; the mean over topics is kept with it, and is what compare_topics() and summary() report.

Coherence is computed from words, while the topics are formed from embeddings, so a topic of short texts that share meaning but not vocabulary can score low. It complements reading the representative texts and does not replace it.

Usage

coherence(
  object,
  measure = c("npmi", "umass"),
  n_terms = 10L,
  smoothing = 1,
  token_lists = NULL,
  cores = 1L,
  weight = c("none", "size")
)

Arguments

object

A topic model fitted by topics().

measure

"npmi" (default) or "umass".

n_terms

Top terms per topic to score (default 10), capped at the terms a topic has.

smoothing

Count added to each co-occurrence count for UMass (default 1).

token_lists

Optional precomputed token lists, one per modeled unit, as held by a topic_corpus(); NULL (default) tokenizes the text. The scores are the same either way.

cores

Number of forked worker processes for tokenization (default 1; Unix-alikes only). Results do not depend on it.

weight

How topic scores are averaged into the mean: "none" (default), every topic equally, or "size", each topic in proportion to its number of units, so that a very small topic of near-identical texts cannot move the mean.

Value

A base data frame with one row per topic and columns topic, label, measure, n_terms (terms scored), and coherence (NA for a topic with fewer than two terms). The mean over the scored topics is attached as the attribute mean_coherence (NA when no topic can be scored) and the averaging as weight; summary() prints the mean.

References

Bouma, G. (2009). Normalized (pointwise) mutual information in collocation extraction. Proceedings of GSCL, 31–40.

Mimno, D., Wallach, H. M., Talley, E., Leenders, M., and McCallum, A. (2011). Optimizing semantic coherence in topic models. Proceedings of EMNLP 2011, 262–272.

See also

topic_diversity(); summary() for the model report; compare_topics() to compare numbers of topics.

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
coherence(topic_model)
#>   topic                                                       label measure
#> 1     1   Where is the cow and the cake? Choose all the pictures...    npmi
#> 2     2            All the ones between the cat and the strawberry.    npmi
#> 3     3         What does “all the ones between the leaf and the...    npmi
#> 4     4 Are you sure you have fewer pictures in the red box than...    npmi
#> 5     5      In the top middle box, it means something is in the...    npmi
#> 6     6    It is not a person, does not have a hat, and is sitting.    npmi
#>   n_terms  coherence
#> 1      10 -0.2367956
#> 2      10 -0.4150297
#> 3      10 -0.2563526
#> 4      10  0.3010516
#> 5      10 -0.2043292
#> 6      10  0.1849079
coherence(topic_model, measure = "umass", weight = "size")
#>   topic                                                       label measure
#> 1     1   Where is the cow and the cake? Choose all the pictures...   umass
#> 2     2            All the ones between the cat and the strawberry.   umass
#> 3     3         What does “all the ones between the leaf and the...   umass
#> 4     4 Are you sure you have fewer pictures in the red box than...   umass
#> 5     5      In the top middle box, it means something is in the...   umass
#> 6     6    It is not a person, does not have a hat, and is sitting.   umass
#>   n_terms coherence
#> 1      10 -2.752499
#> 2      10 -2.657697
#> 3      10 -2.671608
#> 4      10 -1.445615
#> 5      10 -1.897612
#> 6      10 -1.482345
